Question
========
Computer networks exchange data in packets, sent one after the other, separated by a preamble and a period of silence on the wire equivalent to 20 bytes in total.

How many 64 byte packets can a 10 Gbps link send in one second?


Answerlist
----------
* about 14.88 million
* about 19.53 million
* about 1.25 million
* about 10 million

Solution
========
Each packet occupies 64 + 20 = 84 bytes on the wire, that is 672 bits. 10 000 000 000 / 672 gives about 14.88 million packets per second.

Answerlist
----------
* 1. 10e9 divided by (64 + 20) x 8 = 10e9 / 672 = 14 880 952 packets per second.
* 0. This forgets the 20 bytes of inter-packet overhead.
* 0. This divides by 8000 instead of by 672.
* 0. The rate is in bits per second, not in packets per second.
